title: Hazel and the Cipher
premise: Hazel Pemberton has spent a decade as the night concierge of the Marlowe Grand, cataloguing the town's indiscretions in a private ledger no one knows exists. When a confession letter arrives postmarked the day after local magnate Edmund Voss's funeral—naming a witness everyone insists died years ago—Hazel realizes her files hold the key to a murder trial that could topple half the town. As she hunts the living witness through her own alphabetized secrets, she discovers her found family at the hotel is entangled in the cover-up, forcing her to choose between protecting them and telling the truth. In the end, Hazel testifies with her ledger in hand, exposing the killer and losing her invisibility forever—but gaining a family that chooses her back.
about_author: Casper Vane is the pen name of a former hotel night manager who spent years listening to other people's secrets behind a brass bell desk. They write mysteries about quiet observers who know too much.

chapters.title: The Day After
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Ten days after Edmund Voss's funeral, a confession letter arrives at the Marlowe Grand addressed to 'the one who keeps the files.' It references a witness—Mara Quill—declared dead seven years ago. Hazel checks her ledger and finds three entries contradicting the official record. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in the comfort of routine beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Alphabet of Sins
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She rereads her decade of ledgers and reconstructs the night Mara Quill supposedly drowned, finding gaps where pages were removed—by someone with access to her room. Her protégé, bellhop Theo, lies about being on shift that week. Emotional beat: the horror of realizing her sanctuary was breached by someone she trusts.

chapters.title: What the Bell Desk Hears
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with an interlude from Theo's journal. She quietly interviews longtime staff under the guise of scheduling, learning that Voss visited the hotel the night before his death asking for 'the girl who used to work summers.' The head housekeeper, Ida, warns her to stop digging. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling against curiosity.

chapters.title: A Witness, Presumed
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Following a payroll discrepancy she once filed away, Hazel traces Mara Quill to a coastal town two hours north—and finds the trail freshly disturbed; someone else got there first. A slashed tire on her return signals she's being watched. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Trial Calendar
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The district attorney subpoenas hotel records for Voss's murder trial, set to begin in three weeks. Hazel must decide whether to surrender her ledgers, which implicate both the innocent and the guilty. Theo confesses he removed pages—but only to protect Ida. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as desperate protection.

chapters.title: Ida's Room 214
chapters.summary: Ida's POV. Flashback chapter: seven years ago, Ida saw what happened to Mara Quill and was paid to forget, the hush money laundered through the hotel's books—the very entries Hazel filed without understanding. Present-day Ida begs Hazel to let the dead stay dead. Emotional beat: grief and complicity, the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: Salt and Static
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In the coastal town, Hazel finds Mara alive under a new name—alive because she faked her death to escape Voss, who killed her brother. But Mara refuses to testify unless Hazel proves who sent the confession letter, suspecting a trap. Someone follows Hazel home. Emotional beat: hope shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: The Confession's Author
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Forensic details in the letter match the typewriter in the hotel's forgotten mezzanine office—used by Voss himself before his death. He mailed it deliberately, a dead man's revenge designed to detonate at trial. Hazel realizes whoever is threatening her wants the letter buried before it surfaces. Emotional beat: vertigo—she's a pawn in a plot older than her investigation.

chapters.title: Night Audit
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The killer—Ida's silent partner, the hotel's owner Gerald Ashcombe, who covered up Mara's 'death' to protect Voss's empire—confronts Hazel in the lobby after hours, demanding the ledgers. Theo and Ida arrive; Ida turns witness against Ashcombe to save them all. A violent struggle ends with Ashcombe arrested. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into solidarity.

chapters.title: Check-Out
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, closing with Mara's testimony. At trial, Hazel surrenders her ledgers and testifies; Mara takes the stand, alive, and the truth finally outs. Hazel loses her anonymity—her name in every paper—but gains something better: a family that stayed. Final image: she retires the first ledger, opens a fresh page, and writes nothing but tomorrow's date. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace, the price paid and worth it.
